A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same experiment-guided AlphaFold3 study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original crystallographic density-fitting experiments, NMR restraint and flexibility evaluations, and ubiquitin order-parameter results in Tables A1–A4 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, expanded protein evaluations, runtime measurements, and an ensemble-pruning ablation.

M1.justification: The likelihoods, guided diffusion procedure, structural filtering and relaxation, and matching-pursuit selection remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the five-conformer selection cap are retained; the new noise-model explanation and pruning analysis do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Table A9 adds 15 crystallographic cases, including longer alternative-conformation regions and complete short polypeptide chains. Table A10 broadens NMR coverage to proteins up to 353 residues. Its 27 rows include 24 previously unlisted proteins and three repeated targets, rather than 27 entirely new proteins.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated AlphaFlow and ESMFlow comparisons to the retained NMR and crystallographic benchmarks in Tables A7–A8 and Figure A3. Guided Chroma is added in Table A8, and both guided and unguided Chroma appear in Figure A4. These substantially expand the original AlphaFold3, PDB, and guidance-variant comparisons.

E3.justification: New experiments measure runtime at NMR ensemble sizes 16, 32, 64, and 128 and examine pruning sizes from 1 to 10. Table A10 also reports different restraint counts for repeated targets, such as 993 for 2JRM versus 2706 in the retained Table A4, without explaining their selection. Existing preprocessing, guidance settings, and principal metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure A6 adds an explicit test of how selected ensemble size affects density fit, supporting the existing five-conformer cap. Tables A5–A6 add computational-cost and scaling analyses, while Figures A3–A4 extend the bimodality analysis to alternative ensemble generators. These provide substantial additional scrutiny of practical efficiency and ensemble behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five independent ubiquitin runs and retain the diffusion-trajectory confidence bands. New Figure A6 contains shaded bands, but neither its caption nor Appendix A.8 defines their statistical meaning. Whether it introduces additional uncertainty reporting cannot be determined reliably.

E6.justification: Tables A5–A10 add extensive runtime, comparator, and additional-protein results. The retained Table A3 changes the PDB score for 2O1A from 0.749 to 0.759, reversing its ranking against the unchanged guided score of 0.757. The bimodality distributions also change between v1 Figure A1 and v2 Figure A2. Tables A1, A2, and A4 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.2 explicitly specifies probabilistic noise assumptions: unit-scale Laplace density errors, a flat NOE region with quadratic tails, and isotropic Gaussian substructure errors. This adds formal specification underlying the existing losses; the principal equations and derivations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims about experimental posterior guidance, conformational heterogeneity, improved experimental agreement, and computational efficiency. The conclusion retains the same scope and future extensions. Additional evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly acknowledges that the density-noise approximation omits the physics of noise introduced through Fourier intensities. Appendix A.8 adds an overfitting explanation for limiting selected ensembles to five conformers. The related-work discussion also attributes Chroma limitations to its hierarchy and weaker sequence conditioning.

D1.justification: Tables A5–A6 and Appendix A.4 add concrete runtime information tied to protein and ensemble sizes. The expanded evaluations document target regions and restraint counts. The existing Protenix implementation disclosure, official AlphaFold3 baseline, GPU types, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 7 substantially expands positioning against experimental structure and ensemble methods, including Fadini, Liu, Maddipatla, Levy, and Toth-Petroczy and colleagues. It distinguishes their modalities, conditioning, and heterogeneity capabilities from this work. This goes beyond the limited prior positioning in v1.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact. v2 adds Related Work, Acknowledgments, and three appendix subsections, with localized explanatory edits and updated cross-references. Author contribution markings, correspondence details, and conference publication information also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables and three figures and reorganizes the supplementary displays. Former main-text Figures 5 and 7 become appendix Figures A1 and A7. The bimodality plot is redrawn with reordered targets and revised legends, and appendix figures are grouped separately from their explanatory text.

improvement.justification: The broader comparator evidence, measured runtimes, and pruning ablation make the unchanged method easier to assess. However, new summaries overstate the tables: Section 5 claims all added crystallographic cases match or exceed PDB fits, whereas Table A9 supports this for only four of fifteen; Appendix A.3 likewise claims universal superiority despite counterexamples in Table A8. Unexplained restraint-count differences and inconsistent overlapping density scores further limit confidence. The additions provide a useful but qualified net improvement.
